key_insight: GINNGER learns thermodynamic generators rather than constitutive operators, yielding complex-fluid models that satisfy the first and second laws of thermodynamics by construction.
engineering_relevance: A single physically constrained constitutive model can support predictions across deformation protocols and flow geometries without prescribing phenomenological equations in advance.
method: Learn underlying thermodynamic generators from microstructural flow data using the GENERIC formalism.
Represent microstructural state in the polymer conformation tensor’s intrinsic eigenspace.
Treat flow kinematics as an external driver, combining shear, extensional, and mixed-flow data.
evidence_signal: Validation using high-fidelity simulations reports accurate constitutive reconstruction and complex-flow predictions in previously unseen geometries.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative error metrics or experimental validation, leaving real-material accuracy and robustness to measurement noise unresolved.
paper_title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
